bands.title: Battery capacity is low
bands.summary: Battery retains approximately {value}% of design capacity.
bands.action: Plan a battery replacement.

bands.title: Battery capacity reduced
bands.summary: Battery retains approximately {value}% of design capacity.
bands.action: Monitor battery condition. Replacement is not yet urgent.

bands.title: Battery in good condition
bands.summary: Battery retains approximately {value}% of design capacity.

bands.title: Drive has reached its rated life
bands.summary: {item} reports {value}% of rated life used.
bands.action: Back up important files and replace the drive.

bands.title: Drive wear is high
bands.summary: {item} reports {value}% of rated life used.
bands.action: Plan a drive replacement. Failure timing cannot be predicted precisely; back up important files.

bands.title: Drive wear is low
bands.summary: {item} reports {value}% of rated life used.

bands.title: Drive spare capacity is almost gone
bands.summary: {item} has {value}% spare capacity left.
bands.action: Back up important files and replace the drive.

bands.title: Drive spare capacity is low
bands.summary: {item} has {value}% spare capacity left.
bands.action: Plan a drive replacement.

bands.title: Drive raised a critical warning
bands.summary: {item} reports a critical warning from its controller.
bands.action: Back up now and replace the drive.

bands.title: Drive recorded data integrity errors
bands.summary: {item} recorded {value} media and data integrity error(s).
bands.action: Data integrity is at risk. Back up, then replace the drive.

bands.title: Windows reports a drive as unhealthy
bands.summary: {item} is reported as Unhealthy.
bands.action: Back up now and replace the drive.

bands.title: Windows reports a drive warning
bands.summary: {item} is reported with a Warning.
bands.action: Verify backups and plan a replacement.

bands.title: Drive reports healthy
bands.summary: {item} is reported as Healthy. No critical SMART warning.

bands.title: Many unsafe shutdowns recorded
bands.summary: {item} recorded {value} unsafe shutdowns: power was lost or the PC was forced off.
bands.action: Repeated hard power-offs risk file corruption. Check the power supply and shut down normally.

bands.title: Storage is almost full
bands.summary: {item} has {value}% free.
bands.action: Free up space before Windows runs short.

bands.title: Storage is nearly full
bands.summary: {item} has {value}% free.
bands.action: Free up space soon.

bands.title: Processor reached a dangerous temperature
bands.summary: The processor reached {value}°C.
bands.action: Stop heavy work and inspect the cooling system.

bands.title: Processor ran hot
bands.summary: The processor reached {value}°C.
bands.action: Run a deeper cooling test.

bands.title: Processor temperature normal
bands.summary: The processor peaked at {value}°C.

bands.title: Cooling problem suspected
bands.summary: The processor reduced its speed to protect itself from heat.
bands.action: Inspect the cooling system before buying other parts.

bands.title: Memory capacity is low
bands.summary: {value} GB of memory is installed.
bands.action: Modern Windows runs best with 8 GB or more.

bands.title: Memory capacity adequate
bands.summary: {value} GB of memory. No immediate issue detected.

bands.title: Security protection is off
bands.summary: Microsoft Defender real-time protection is disabled.
bands.action: Turn protection on, or confirm another security product is active.

bands.title: Security protection is on
bands.summary: Microsoft Defender real-time protection is enabled.

bands.title: Firewall is off
bands.summary: The Windows firewall is disabled.
bands.action: Turn the firewall on unless another one is in use.

bands.title: Drive is not encrypted
bands.summary: The system drive is not protected by BitLocker or device encryption. Anyone holding this PC can read its files.
bands.action: Turn on BitLocker or device encryption, and keep the recovery key somewhere safe.

bands.title: Drive is encrypted
bands.summary: The system drive is protected by BitLocker or device encryption.

bands.title: Secure Boot is off
bands.summary: Windows is not checking that what starts before it is trusted, which is how boot-level malware gets in.
bands.action: Turn on Secure Boot in the PC firmware settings if it is supported.

bands.title: Secure Boot is on
bands.summary: The firmware verifies what starts before Windows.

bands.title: No security chip (TPM) found
bands.summary: Windows reports no TPM. Encryption keys and Windows Hello cannot be hardware-protected.
bands.action: Check the firmware for a TPM or fTPM setting.

bands.title: Security chip (TPM) present
bands.summary: This PC has a TPM for key protection.

bands.title: Windows has not updated in months
bands.summary: The last installed Windows update was {value} day(s) ago.
bands.action: Run Windows Update now. Unpatched Windows is the most common way PCs are compromised.

bands.title: Windows updates are overdue
bands.summary: The last installed Windows update was {value} day(s) ago.
bands.action: Run Windows Update.

bands.title: Windows updates are recent
bands.summary: The last installed Windows update was {value} day(s) ago.

bands.title: A restart is waiting
bands.summary: Windows has installed something that only takes effect after a restart.
bands.action: Save your work and restart.

bands.title: Windows version is out of support
bands.summary: Microsoft ended standard security updates for this Windows version {value} days ago.
bands.action: Upgrade Windows. Paid extended updates may still be available for some versions.

bands.title: Windows version support ends soon
bands.summary: Microsoft ends standard security updates for this Windows version within six months.
bands.action: Plan the move to a supported Windows version.

bands.title: Windows version is supported
bands.summary: This Windows version still receives standard security updates.

bands.title: Virus definitions are out of date
bands.summary: Microsoft Defender definitions are {value} day(s) old.
bands.action: Open Windows Security and update protection definitions.

bands.title: Virus definitions are current
bands.summary: Microsoft Defender definitions are {value} day(s) old.

bands.title: No recent malware scan
bands.summary: Defender has not completed a quick scan in {value} days.
bands.action: Run a quick scan from Windows Security.

bands.title: User Account Control is off
bands.summary: Programs can change the system without asking.
bands.action: Turn User Account Control back on in Windows security settings.

bands.title: Old file-sharing protocol (SMBv1) is on
bands.summary: SMBv1 is the protocol used by well-known ransomware worms.
bands.action: Turn off SMB 1.0 in Windows Features.

bands.title: Remote Desktop is switched on
bands.summary: Other computers can try to sign in to this PC remotely.
bands.action: Turn Remote Desktop off unless you use it.

bands.title: Windows signs in automatically
bands.summary: Anyone who starts this PC reaches the desktop without a password.
bands.action: Require a password at sign-in.

bands.title: Guest account is enabled
bands.summary: The built-in Guest account allows sign-in without a personal account.
bands.action: Disable the Guest account.

bands.title: Windows has crashed repeatedly
bands.summary: Windows logged {value} blue-screen crashes in the last 30 days.
bands.action: Update drivers and check the drive and memory. Repeated crashes usually mean a hardware or driver fault.

bands.title: Windows crashed recently
bands.summary: Windows logged {value} blue-screen crash(es) in the last 30 days.
bands.action: Note when it happened and what you were doing. A second one points to a driver or hardware fault.

bands.title: No blue-screen crashes
bands.summary: No blue-screen crash was logged in the last 30 days.

bands.title: The PC keeps shutting down unexpectedly
bands.summary: Windows logged {value} unexpected shutdowns or power losses in the last 30 days.
bands.action: Check the power supply or battery, and shut down from the Start menu.

bands.title: Windows is logging many disk errors
bands.summary: Windows logged {value} disk errors in the last 30 days.
bands.action: Back up important files now and have the drive checked.

bands.title: Windows logged disk errors
bands.summary: Windows logged {value} disk error(s) in the last 30 days.
bands.action: Back up important files and run a drive health check.

bands.title: No disk errors logged
bands.summary: Windows logged no disk errors in the last 30 days.

bands.title: Programs keep crashing
bands.summary: Windows logged {value} program crashes in the last 30 days.
bands.action: Update or reinstall the program that crashes most.

bands.title: Connected to an open Wi-Fi network
bands.summary: Open networks do not encrypt what this PC sends over Wi-Fi.
bands.action: Use a network with a password, or a VPN.

bands.title: Wi-Fi uses outdated WEP security
bands.summary: WEP can be broken in minutes.
bands.action: Change the router to WPA2 or WPA3.

bands.title: Wi-Fi uses outdated WPA security
bands.summary: Original WPA is weak.
bands.action: Change the router to WPA2 or WPA3.

bands.title: Wi-Fi uses WPA2
bands.summary: The connected Wi-Fi network is encrypted with WPA2.

bands.title: Wi-Fi uses WPA3
bands.summary: The connected Wi-Fi network is encrypted with WPA3.

bands.title: Many programs start with Windows
bands.summary: {value} programs start automatically, which slows start-up and uses memory.
bands.action: Turn off the ones you do not need in Task Manager > Startup.
